strings.name: Pascal Soriot
strings.summary: Trained in veterinary medicine and management, Soriot entered pharmaceuticals through sales and became AstraZeneca CEO in 2012. He led expansion in oncology, the Alexion rare-disease acquisition and Oxford vaccine collaboration. Research, regulation and supply involve many organizations; the company continues to face patent expiries, competition and procurement pressures.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Leads AstraZeneca, developing innovative medicines including oncology and contributing to global medical-product supply.
strings.facts.f1.label: Background
strings.facts.f1.value: Born in France; holds French and Australian citizenship.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Veterinary education at Alfort, France; MBA from HEC Paris.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Innovative-medicine transformation
strings.highlights.h1.text: Led growth in oncology and added rare-disease capabilities through Alexion.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Research and global supply
strings.highlights.h2.text: Organizes partnerships, clinical development and manufacturing networks connecting science with patients.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Nine-month 2026 results
strings.timeline.t1.text: Reported commercial and clinical progress alongside patent and Chinese procurement headwinds.
strings.timeline.t2.title: British knighthood
strings.timeline.t2.text: Recognized for life sciences and leadership in the global COVID-19 response.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Alexion acquisition completed
strings.timeline.t3.text: AstraZeneca entered rare diseases with a complement-biology platform.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Oxford vaccine agreement
strings.timeline.t4.text: Agreed development, manufacturing and distribution of a candidate; authorization did not occur that day.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Became AstraZeneca CEO
strings.timeline.t5.text: Took office on 1 October, beginning a long business and research transformation.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Roche Pharma COO
strings.timeline.t6.text: Moved from Genentech to operational leadership at Roche’s pharmaceuticals division.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Led Genentech
strings.timeline.t7.text: Served as subsidiary CEO during Roche’s integration of the business.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Entered pharmaceutical sales
strings.timeline.t8.text: Joined Roussel Uclaf, starting in sales in Australia.
